note: The elections districtry Illinois tells readers about BEFORE they happen (Adam, 2026-11-15: "I want visitors to know I'll have election results after, in the lead up to the election"). scripts/build_election_notices.py reads this file and writes every place the notice appears: the Next election box on election-results.html, the line in the map's Elections section, the closing line on the candidates page and the polling place card, the front page's line, and the calendar reminder under calendar/. `kind` picks one of three wordings and is the one edit that moves a place between them: "posted" (results will be posted here; allowed only where this app has already posted this office's results from a real election), "plans" (districtry plans to post them; the office publishes a file a program may read and it has not been used in a real election yet), "official" (districtry cannot post them; `why` says why, and the notice links the office's own page). Only regularly scheduled elections belong here, and nothing about a special election. A runoff names the election it follows in `after` and is shown only from the day after it. An entry is shown by the reader's own clock, so nothing here needs editing when election day passes; retire an entry once its results are on the results page.
